name: Egg Tart
description: A flaky pastry shell holding a smooth, barely-set egg custard—a Cantonese bakery staple brought from Portuguese pastéis.
ingredients: a handful of fresh scallion greens, chopped
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with toasted sesame oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the steamed buns and doubanjiang (chili bean paste) until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the oyster sauce with the pork stock until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 20 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with chives or a dusting of black vinegar.
tips: Bring your oyster sauce to room temperature before mixing for a smoother, more even texture.
Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
